synopsis: Across the corpus, prototype hardware and software are expected in mid-2027, with validation required in less than four months; Chapter 12 describes about seven months, October 2026–April 2027, for preparing virtual-testing capability [f3, f1173, f9402, f11338]. Comparable functions previously required three to four years of mostly physical testing and per-model tuning, and the research found no documented case proving full validation of a new machine family in about four months [f2030, f4391, f1255, f7350]. Expert opinion makes feasibility conditional on completing simulation credibility and sensor-model validation before prototype arrival, so the final window should confirm preparations, correlate models and resolve discrepancies rather than establish the methodology [f7591, f4458, f5614, f7593, f11342]. The proposed route combines an analytical safety case, credibility-framed simulation and targeted physical tests, but this evidence plan is a research-derived recommendation, not a requirement imposed by the sources; completing the indicative physical matrix also depends on shared instrumentation across machine families [f2137, f2637, f6178]. Important constraints remain: the window excludes northern cold-season conditions, finite simulation capacity forces selective high-fidelity testing, and the research does not establish that testing volume caused the historical three-to-four-year duration [f4403, f10460, f8871, f10394].
